findings.title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && so it can never be true
findings.body: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))`. A membership in Cal.com has a single role, so a user cannot simultaneously be ADMIN and OWNER of the same team — this expression is always false. As a result, team admins and team owners (whom the UI explicitly allows to manage the booking via `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner` in BookingListItem) will always hit the FORBIDDEN branch and cannot add guests. The two checks should be combined with `||`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The handler builds the EventManager from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, i.e. the credentials and identity of whoever clicked "add guests". But the permission check explicitly allows attendees and team admins to call this endpoint, and the calendar event being updated belongs to the booking organizer (`booking.user`). When anyone other than the organizer adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs with credentials that have no access to the organizer's calendar, so the calendar event is never updated with the new attendees (or the call fails). Note the booking query already includes `booking.user.credentials` but they are never used — the organizer's credentials/user should be used to construct the EventManager.

findings.title: No booking status check — guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
findings.body: After fetching the booking, the handler only checks permissions; it never verifies `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`. The UI only shows the action for confirmed bookings, but the tRPC mutation is directly callable, so any attendee can add guests to a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking (or one that already ended), creating Attendee rows and triggering confirmation/ICS emails with method REQUEST for a dead event. The handler should reject bookings that are not ACCEPTED (and arguably those already in the past).

findings.title: Case-sensitive duplicate/blacklist comparison lets duplicate attendees in and breaks the blacklist
findings.body: The dedupe filter compares `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` with exact string equality. The blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is not, so `Foo@Bar.com` on the blacklist is never matched. Worse, if the booking already has attendee `foo@bar.com` and someone submits `Foo@Bar.com`, the filter passes and `createMany` inserts a second attendee row for the same person (email uniqueness in the DB is case-sensitive), producing duplicate attendees who then both receive emails and calendar updates. Emails should be normalized (trimmed/lowercased) before comparison and before insert.

findings.title: Raw `guests` (not `uniqueGuests`) passed to sendAddGuestsEmails sends the wrong template
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw input array, not the deduplicated `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, each attendee gets the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` if `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, otherwise the "guests added" notification. So if the requester includes an email that is already an attendee (filtered out of `uniqueGuests`, not re-added), that existing attendee incorrectly receives a brand-new booking confirmation email instead of the notification. Conversely, because the matching is case-sensitive, a genuinely new guest stored with different casing than the input gets the notification template instead of the confirmation. Pass `uniqueGuests` and compare normalized emails.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email opt-out settings
findings.body: Every other send function in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, sendCancelledEmails, etc.) accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and skips host/attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` is set, and also strips `additionalNotes` when `hideCalendarNotes` is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata parameter and unconditionally emails the organizer, all team members, and all attendees. Event types that disabled standard emails (a documented privacy feature, e.g. when workflows replace them) will still send these notifications, and hidden calendar notes can leak to attendees.

findings.title: No upper bound on guests array enables email spam abuse
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and no `.min(1)`. Since the handler permits any existing attendee (not just the organizer) to call this mutation, anyone who attended a booking can submit hundreds of arbitrary email addresses, creating hundreds of Attendee rows and causing Cal.com to send organizer-branded invitation emails (with ICS attachments and reply-to set to the organizer) to all of them. Add a reasonable `.max()` (and `.min(1)`) to the schema.

findings.title: Attendees added to seated events without BookingSeat references
findings.body: The handler copies `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` into the CalendarEvent, so seated event types reach this code, but it inserts attendees with a plain `createMany` and never creates the `BookingSeat` reference rows that seated bookings require to track occupancy and to let the attendee manage/reschedule their seat. For a seated event this corrupts seat accounting (the new attendee occupies no seat) and breaks flows that rely on `seatsReferences`. The handler should either reject bookings whose event type has `seatsPerTimeSlot` set, or create proper seat references.

findings.title: Validation error message never clears when the user edits emails
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true when validation fails, but nothing resets it when the user subsequently edits or removes email fields — it is only cleared on cancel or successful submit. A user who fixes the offending address still sees "Emails must be unique and valid" until they click Add again, which is confusing. Clear the flag in the `setValue` path (e.g. wrap `setMultiEmailValue` to also reset `isInvalidEmail`).
